page.layout: One printed page, framed by a decorative woodcut border. Running head at top centre with page number at top right; text in one column; catchword/signature line "D 4" at foot of text block. Partial text of the facing page is visible at the far left edge, outside the frame, and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: Mineral. cap. 7. cùm in hæc verba scribit: Hoc in se omnino verum est, si auri sulphur projicitur in argentum, colorat quidem illud, sed non figit, quod & Basilius innuit, in repetitione Lapidis magni pag. 113.

Rectè igitur Sendivogius in Tractatu 9. de commixtione metallorum: Noverunt (inquit) Chymistæ ferrum in cuprum seu Venerem sine Sole transmutare: sed si scirent (addit) his mutationibus Solis administrare Naturam, certè rem omni thesauro invenirent pretiosiorem. Quid hoc, obsecro, est aliud quam non aurum commune, sed aurum nostrum Philosophicum, ex quo Tinctura Solis, thesaurus pretiosissimus potest postea præparari? Propterea (inquit) dico non ignorandum esse, quæ metalla invi-cem

page.notes: Marginal text on the left outside the frame belongs to the facing page and is not transcribed. The word "cem" at the foot is the catchword, shown after the signature. Reading of "Mineral." and "Sendivogius" follows the printed italic and roman forms as seen.
